nodes.name: Eurostat - Statistical Office of the European Union
nodes.description: Eurostat is the statistical office of the European Union, located in Luxembourg. It is responsible for providing high-quality statistics and data about Europe, coordinating the European Statistical System (ESS), and setting methodological standards and frameworks for statistical production across EU and EEA member states. Eurostat does not collect primary data itself but coordinates with and compiles data from the national statistical institutes (NSIs) of member states. Eurostat is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations and plays a central role in international statistical cooperation, particularly through the Conference of European Statisticians (CES) and cooperation with UNSD, IMF, OECD, and other international bodies. Eurostat promotes the European Statistics Code of Practice (ESCoP) as the quality framework for the ESS.
nodes.summary: Statistical office of the EU; coordinates the ESS; sets methodological standards; SDMX sponsor; promotes ESCoP across 30+ NSIs

nodes.name: ESS - European Statistical System
nodes.description: The European Statistical System (ESS) is the partnership between Eurostat and the national statistical institutes (NSIs) and other national authorities responsible for the development, production and dissemination of European statistics in EU and EEA member states. The ESS functions as a network in which Eurostat's role is to lead the way in the harmonisation of statistics in close cooperation with the national statistical authorities. The ESS is governed by Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 on European statistics and the European Statistics Code of Practice (ESCoP).
nodes.summary: Partnership between Eurostat and 30+ NSIs across EU/EEA; governed by Regulation 223/2009 and ESCoP

nodes.name: International Statistical Bodies
nodes.description: A grouping node representing the international organisations with close working relationships with Eurostat and the ESS on statistical standards, methodologies and data exchange. Includes the seven SDMX sponsors (Eurostat, ECB, IMF, OECD, UN, World Bank, BIS) and specialised UN agencies active in specific statistical domains.
nodes.summary: International organisations cooperating with the ESS on statistical standards, methods and data

nodes.name: UNSD - United Nations Statistics Division
nodes.description: The United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD) is the central mechanism for global statistical coordination. It maintains international classifications (ISIC, CPC), the System of National Accounts (SNA), and manages the global SDMX programme. UNSD jointly secretaries the Conference of European Statisticians (CES) with UNECE and co-develops key frameworks such as GSBPM and CSPA.
nodes.summary: Central UN statistics body; maintains SNA, ISIC, CPC; co-secretaries CES with UNECE; co-develops GSBPM

nodes.name: IMF - International Monetary Fund (Statistics)
nodes.description: The IMF Statistics Department develops international statistical standards including BPM6 (Balance of Payments Manual), the Government Finance Statistics Manual (GFSM) and monetary statistics frameworks. The IMF is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations and cooperates with Eurostat on national accounts and macroeconomic statistics.
nodes.summary: Develops BPM6, GFSM and monetary statistics standards; one of the seven SDMX sponsors

nodes.name: OECD - Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (Statistics)
nodes.description: The OECD cooperates with Eurostat and the broader ESS on business statistics, innovation, R&D and price statistics. It co-publishes the Frascati and Oslo Manuals, conducts the International Comparison Programme (PPP) jointly with Eurostat, and is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations. OECD engages actively in CES working groups and METIS.
nodes.summary: Key partner on Frascati/Oslo manuals, PPP, SDMX and CES working groups; one of the seven SDMX sponsors

nodes.name: ECB - European Central Bank (Statistics)
nodes.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) cooperates with Eurostat on monetary, financial and balance of payments statistics via the ESS-ESCB Memorandum of Understanding. The ECB is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations and participates in the Committee on Monetary, Financial and Balance of Payments Statistics (CMFB).
nodes.summary: Euro area central bank; SDMX sponsor; cooperates with Eurostat on monetary and financial statistics via ESS-ESCB MoU

nodes.name: BIS - Bank for International Settlements (Statistics)
nodes.description: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations and cooperates with the international statistical community on financial and monetary statistics, particularly banking, securities and derivatives data.
nodes.summary: One of the seven SDMX sponsors; cooperates on financial and monetary statistics

nodes.name: World Bank (Development Data)
nodes.description: The World Bank is one of the seven SDMX sponsor organisations and cooperates with Eurostat and the ESS on development data and the International Comparison Programme (ICP/PPP). The World Bank engages with EU member states on statistical capacity building.
nodes.summary: One of the seven SDMX sponsors; cooperates on development data, ICP/PPP and statistical capacity building

nodes.name: FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization (Statistics)
nodes.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) cooperates with Eurostat and the ESS on agricultural statistics, fisheries, food security and forestry data. FAO co-develops SEEA ecosystem accounting frameworks and agricultural census methodology.
nodes.summary: UN food and agriculture agency; cooperates with Eurostat on agricultural, fisheries, forestry and SEEA statistics

nodes.name: ILO - International Labour Organization (Statistics)
nodes.description: The International Labour Organization (ILO) maintains ISCO-08 (International Standard Classification of Occupations) and ICSE-18, and cooperates with Eurostat on labour force survey methodology and international labour market data comparability. The ILO engages actively in the CES working groups on labour statistics.
nodes.summary: UN labour agency; maintains ISCO-08 and ICSE-18; cooperates with Eurostat on LFS methodology and labour market data

nodes.name: WHO - World Health Organization (Statistics)
nodes.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) cooperates with Eurostat on ICD-11, health expenditure (SHA), causes of death data and population health surveys. WHO data feeds into Eurostat health statistics domain.
nodes.summary: UN health agency; maintains ICD-11; co-collects health expenditure (SHA) and causes of death with Eurostat

nodes.name: Statistik Austria
nodes.description: Statistik Austria is the national statistical institute of Austria, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Austria and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates. It participates in ESS working groups and collaborative initiatives.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Austria; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: Statbel - Statistics Belgium
nodes.description: Statbel (Statistics Belgium / Statistique Belgique) is the national statistical institute of Belgium, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Belgium and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Belgium; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: NSI Bulgaria - National Statistical Institute
nodes.description: The National Statistical Institute of Bulgaria (NSI) is responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Bulgaria and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates. It participates in ESS collaborative initiatives and working groups.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Bulgaria; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: DZS - Croatian Bureau of Statistics
nodes.description: The Croatian Bureau of Statistics (CBS / Državni zavod za statistiku) is the national statistical institute of Croatia, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Croatia and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Croatia; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: CYSTAT - Statistical Service of Cyprus
nodes.description: The Statistical Service of Cyprus (CYSTAT) is the national statistical institute of Cyprus, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Cyprus and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Cyprus; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: CZSO - Czech Statistical Office
nodes.description: The Czech Statistical Office (CZSO / Český statistický úřad) is the national statistical institute of the Czech Republic, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics and contributing data to Eurostat. It is an active participant in ESS working groups and modernisation projects.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of the Czech Republic; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: Danmarks Statistik - Statistics Denmark
nodes.description: Statistics Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) is the national statistical institute of Denmark, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Denmark and contributing data to Eurostat. It is known for its advanced use of administrative registers for statistical production.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Denmark; ESS member; known for register-based statistical production

nodes.name: Statistics Estonia (Statistikaamet)
nodes.description: Statistics Estonia (Statistikaamet) is the national statistical institute of Estonia, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Estonia and contributing data to Eurostat. Estonia is internationally recognised for its advanced digital infrastructure and e-government integration in statistical production.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Estonia; ESS member; known for digital and e-government integration in statistics

nodes.name: Statistics Finland (Tilastokeskus)
nodes.description: Statistics Finland (Tilastokeskus) is the national statistical institute of Finland, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Finland and contributing data to Eurostat. Statistics Finland actively participates in ESS modernisation projects and international statistical cooperation.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Finland; ESS member; active in ESS modernisation and international cooperation

nodes.name: INSEE - Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques
nodes.description: INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques) is the national statistical institute of France. It is one of the largest and most influential NSIs in the ESS, responsible for producing official statistics for France and contributing data to Eurostat. INSEE is known for its advanced econometric and modelling capabilities.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of France; one of the largest NSIs in the ESS; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: Destatis - Federal Statistical Office Germany
nodes.description: Destatis (Statistisches Bundesamt / Federal Statistical Office Germany) is the national statistical institute of Germany, one of the largest and most influential NSIs in the ESS. Destatis coordinates a federated German statistical system with statistical offices in each of the 16 Länder and contributes major datasets to Eurostat.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Germany; one of the largest NSIs in the ESS; coordinates a federated national statistical system across 16 Länder

nodes.name: ELSTAT - Hellenic Statistical Authority
nodes.description: ELSTAT (Hellenic Statistical Authority) is the national statistical institute of Greece, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Greece and contributing data to Eurostat. ELSTAT was established in 2010 as an independent authority following concerns about the independence of Greek official statistics.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Greece; ESS member; independent authority established 2010

nodes.name: KSH - Hungarian Central Statistical Office
nodes.description: KSH (Központi Statisztikai Hivatal / Hungarian Central Statistical Office) is the national statistical institute of Hungary, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Hungary and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Hungary; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: CSO - Central Statistics Office Ireland
nodes.description: The Central Statistics Office Ireland (CSO) is the national statistical institute of Ireland. CSO is highly active in ESS collaborative projects, including as lead of the AIML4OS initiative under ESSnet. It is known for its open data policies and modern statistical infrastructure.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Ireland; ESS member; leads AIML4OS initiative; known for open data and modern infrastructure

nodes.name: Istat - National Institute of Statistics Italy
nodes.description: Istat (Istituto Nazionale di Statistica / National Institute of Statistics Italy) is the national statistical institute of Italy and one of the largest NSIs in the ESS. Istat produces official statistics for Italy and contributes major datasets to Eurostat, and is active in ESS modernisation and collaborative projects.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Italy; one of the largest NSIs in the ESS; active in modernisation and collaborative projects

nodes.name: CSB Latvia - Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia
nodes.description: The Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia (CSB / Centrālā statistikas pārvalde) is the national statistical institute of Latvia, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Latvia and contributing data to Eurostat.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Latvia; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: Statistics Lithuania
nodes.description: Statistics Lithuania (Oficialiosios statistikos portalas) is the national statistical institute of Lithuania, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Lithuania and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Lithuania; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: STATEC - Statistics Luxembourg
nodes.description: STATEC (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) is the national statistical institute of Luxembourg, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Luxembourg and contributing data to Eurostat.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Luxembourg; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: NSO - National Statistics Office Malta
nodes.description: The National Statistics Office Malta (NSO) is the national statistical institute of Malta, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Malta and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Malta; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: CBS - Statistics Netherlands
nodes.description: Statistics Netherlands (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / CBS) is the national statistical institute of the Netherlands and one of the most innovative NSIs in the ESS. CBS is known for its work on big data, data science and privacy-preserving technologies, and is active in international statistical modernisation including HLG-MOS.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of the Netherlands; ESS member; known for big data, data science and privacy-preserving statistics; active in HLG-MOS

nodes.name: GUS - Statistics Poland
nodes.description: Statistics Poland (Główny Urząd Statystyczny / GUS) is the national statistical institute of Poland and one of the larger NSIs in the ESS. GUS produces official statistics for Poland and contributes major datasets to Eurostat, and is active in ESS collaborative initiatives.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Poland; one of the larger NSIs in the ESS; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: INE Portugal - Statistics Portugal
nodes.description: Statistics Portugal (Instituto Nacional de Estatística / INE Portugal) is the national statistical institute of Portugal, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Portugal and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Portugal; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: INS Romania - National Institute of Statistics
nodes.description: The National Institute of Statistics Romania (INS / Institutul Național de Statistică) is the national statistical institute of Romania, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Romania and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Romania; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: ŠÚSR - Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
nodes.description: The Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic (Štatistický úrad Slovenskej republiky / ŠÚ SR) is the national statistical institute of Slovakia, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Slovakia and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Slovakia; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: SURS - Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia
nodes.description: The Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia (Statistični urad Republike Slovenije / SURS) is the national statistical institute of Slovenia, responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Slovenia and contributing data to Eurostat for European aggregates.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Slovenia; ESS member; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: INE Spain - National Statistics Institute
nodes.description: The National Statistics Institute of Spain (Instituto Nacional de Estadística / INE Spain) is the national statistical institute of Spain and one of the larger NSIs in the ESS. INE Spain produces official statistics for Spain and contributes major datasets to Eurostat.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Spain; one of the larger NSIs in the ESS; contributes to Eurostat and EU statistics

nodes.name: SCB - Statistics Sweden
nodes.description: Statistics Sweden (Statistiska centralbyrån / SCB) is the national statistical institute of Sweden. SCB is one of the most prominent NSIs in the ESS, with a long tradition of register-based statistics and advanced data integration. It is active in international statistical cooperation, ESS modernisation projects, and HLG-MOS activities including the Trust Matters project.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Sweden; ESS member; known for register-based statistics and data integration; active in HLG-MOS and ESS modernisation

nodes.name: Statistics Iceland (Hagstofa Íslands)
nodes.description: Statistics Iceland (Hagstofa Íslands) is the national statistical institute of Iceland and an EEA member of the ESS. It is responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Iceland and contributing data to Eurostat under the EEA Agreement.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Iceland; EEA member of the ESS; contributes to Eurostat under EEA Agreement

nodes.name: Amt für Statistik - Office for Statistics Liechtenstein
nodes.description: The Office for Statistics Liechtenstein (Amt für Statistik) is the national statistical authority of Liechtenstein and an EEA member of the ESS. It is responsible for producing and disseminating official statistics for Liechtenstein and contributing data to Eurostat under the EEA Agreement.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Liechtenstein; EEA member of the ESS; contributes to Eurostat under EEA Agreement

nodes.name: SSB - Statistics Norway
nodes.description: Statistics Norway (Statistisk sentralbyrå / SSB) is the national statistical institute of Norway and an EEA member of the ESS. SSB is one of the most advanced and well-resourced NSIs in the EEA, known for register-based statistics, data science innovation and active participation in international statistical cooperation including HLG-MOS.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Norway; EEA member of the ESS; known for register-based statistics and data science innovation

nodes.name: FSO - Federal Statistical Office Switzerland
nodes.description: The Federal Statistical Office of Switzerland (Bundesamt für Statistik / BFS; Office fédéral de la statistique / OFS) cooperates closely with Eurostat and the ESS despite Switzerland not being an EU or EEA member. Cooperation is governed by bilateral statistical agreements. FSO participates in a number of ESS collaborative projects and contributes data for selected European statistics domains.
nodes.summary: National statistical institute of Switzerland; cooperates with Eurostat via bilateral statistical agreements; participates in selected ESS projects

nodes.name: Labour Force Surveys (LFS)
nodes.description: Statistics describing labour market conditions and labour market trends in Sweden. The Labour Force Surveys (LFS) cover the population aged 15–74 and are based on a sample survey of approximately 29,500 persons per month. Results describe employment, unemployment, and persons not in the labour force, and are published monthly. LFS is the main source for Swedish official labour market statistics and feeds into Eurostat's EU-LFS harmonised dataset.
nodes.summary: Monthly Swedish labour market survey covering population aged 15–74; main source for employment, unemployment and inactivity statistics

nodes.name: Monthly labour market status by region, sex and age
nodes.description: Aggregated monthly LFS dataset showing labour market status by demographic and regional breakdowns. Each observation represents an estimated number of persons in a given labour market status, disaggregated by region, sex, age group and reference month. Data are published monthly by Statistics Sweden and contribute to Eurostat's EU-LFS harmonised tables.
nodes.summary: Monthly LFS dataset: labour market status broken down by region, sex, age group and month

nodes.name: Population aged 15-74 by region, labour status and sex
nodes.description: Annual aggregated LFS dataset showing population aged 15–74 by region, labour status and sex. Covers the period 2005–2025 and is published in the Statistics Sweden statistical database. Each observation represents an estimated annual average number of persons in a given labour market status, disaggregated by region and sex.
nodes.summary: Annual LFS dataset: population 15–74 by region, labour status and sex; covers 2005–2025

nodes.name: Labour market status table structure
nodes.description: Common data structure for aggregated LFS tables broken down by region, sex, age group, labour market status and time period. The structure is multidimensional with five identifier variables (region, sex, age_group, labour_status, time_period) and one measure variable (population_count). Both the monthly and annual LFS aggregate datasets share this structure.
nodes.summary: Shared data structure for LFS aggregate tables: 5 identifiers (region, sex, age group, labour status, time) + 1 measure (population count)

nodes.name: region
nodes.description: Geographical region used for breakdown of labour market statistics. Coded variable using a regional classification (e.g. NUTS regions for Sweden). Acts as an identifier dimension in the LFS aggregate table structure.
nodes.summary: Geographical region; identifier dimension in LFS tables; coded using regional classification

nodes.name: sex
nodes.description: Sex of the person, used as a demographic breakdown in LFS aggregate tables. Coded variable with values for men and women. Acts as an identifier dimension in the LFS aggregate table structure.
nodes.summary: Sex; demographic identifier dimension in LFS tables; coded (men/women)

nodes.name: age_group
nodes.description: Age group used for presentation of labour market statistics. Persons are grouped into age bands (e.g. 15–24, 25–54, 55–74 years) for LFS aggregate tables. Acts as an identifier dimension.
nodes.summary: Age group; identifier dimension in LFS tables; coded age bands (15–24, 25–54, 55–74)

nodes.name: labour_status
nodes.description: Classification of persons by labour market status: employed, unemployed, or not in the labour force. Coded variable following ILO definitions as adapted for the EU-LFS framework. Acts as a key identifier dimension in the LFS aggregate table structure.
nodes.summary: Labour market status; key identifier dimension; coded (employed / unemployed / not in labour force)

nodes.name: time_period
nodes.description: Reference month or year for the observation. For the monthly dataset this is the calendar month; for the annual dataset this is the reference year. Acts as an identifier dimension providing the time axis in the LFS aggregate table structure.
nodes.summary: Time period; identifier dimension; reference month or year for the LFS observation

nodes.name: population_count
nodes.description: Estimated number of persons in the specified labour market status and demographic/regional breakdown. This is the single measure variable in the LFS aggregate table structure. Expressed in persons (thousands in published tables).
nodes.summary: Number of persons; measure variable in LFS tables; estimated population count in the specified breakdown

nodes.name: Region
nodes.description: A geographical area used for statistical classification and dissemination. In Swedish LFS, regions correspond to counties (län) and NUTS-level aggregations.
nodes.summary: Geographical area used for statistical classification and breakdown

nodes.name: Sex
nodes.description: A demographic characteristic used to classify persons as men or women. In Swedish LFS, sex is collected and reported according to registered sex.
nodes.summary: Demographic characteristic classifying persons by sex

nodes.name: Age
nodes.description: The age of a person, usually grouped for statistical presentation. In LFS, persons aged 15–74 are covered and grouped into standard age bands.
nodes.summary: Age of a person; grouped into age bands for LFS statistical presentation

nodes.name: Labour market status
nodes.description: A person's status in relation to the labour market. Defined according to ILO standards and adapted for EU-LFS: employed persons are those who worked at least one hour in the reference week; unemployed persons are without work, available and seeking; all others are not in the labour force.
nodes.summary: Classification of a person's relationship to the labour market: employed, unemployed or not in the labour force (ILO definition)

nodes.name: Population count
nodes.description: The estimated number of persons in a defined statistical category. In LFS tables, population counts are survey-based estimates of the number of persons in the target population belonging to a given category.
nodes.summary: Estimated number of persons in a defined statistical category; survey-based estimate

nodes.name: Person
nodes.description: An individual human being observed or represented in labour market statistics. All LFS aggregate tables have the person as the unit of observation.
nodes.summary: Individual human being; unit of observation in LFS statistics

nodes.name: Sex code list (LFS demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for sex in the LFS demo scenario.
nodes.summary: Sex codes: 1=Men, 2=Women

nodes.name: Labour market status code list (LFS demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for labour market status in the LFS scenario, based on ILO definitions as applied in the EU-LFS.
nodes.summary: Labour status codes: EMP=Employed, UNE=Unemployed, NLF=Not in the labour force

nodes.name: LFS age group code list (demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for age groups in the LFS scenario.
nodes.summary: Age group codes: 15–24, 25–54, 55–74 years

nodes.name: Region code list (LFS demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for regions in the LFS scenario, based on Swedish NUTS/county codes.
nodes.summary: Region codes: SE=Sweden, SE11=Stockholm, SE12=East Middle Sweden

nodes.name: Party Preference Survey (PSU)
nodes.description: Statistics describing political party preferences and estimated election results if a parliamentary election were held today. The Party Preference Survey (PSU) is conducted twice yearly by Statistics Sweden and covers the electorate in Sweden. Results are published as estimated vote shares by party and breakdowns by sex, age group, region and employment status. Next publication: 2026-06-04.
nodes.summary: Twice-yearly survey of Swedish political party preferences and election-day estimates; covers electorate by party, sex, age, region and employment status

nodes.name: Election today estimate by party
nodes.description: Aggregated survey dataset showing estimated vote shares by political party if a parliamentary election were held today. Each observation represents an estimated percentage of votes for a given party in a given survey wave. Includes margin of error. Published twice yearly by Statistics Sweden.
nodes.summary: PSU dataset: estimated vote shares by party if election held today; includes margin of error per survey wave

nodes.name: Political party preference by sex, age and region
nodes.description: Aggregated survey dataset showing political party preference broken down by demographic and regional groups. Each observation represents an estimated share of the electorate preferring a given party, disaggregated by sex, age group and region for a given survey wave. Includes margin of error.
nodes.summary: PSU dataset: party preference shares broken down by sex, age group and region per survey wave

nodes.name: Election today estimate table structure
nodes.description: Data structure for aggregated estimates of vote share by political party and survey wave. Contains two identifier variables (political_party, survey_wave) and two measure variables (vote_share_percent, margin_of_error). Used by the Election today estimate dataset.
nodes.summary: Structure for PSU election-today table: 2 identifiers (party, survey wave) + 2 measures (vote share %, margin of error)

nodes.name: Party preference by demographic group table structure
nodes.description: Data structure for aggregated party preference estimates broken down by party, sex, age group, region and survey wave. Contains five identifier variables and two measure variables (preference_share_percent, margin_of_error). Used by the party preference by demographic group dataset.
nodes.summary: Structure for PSU demographic breakdown table: 5 identifiers (party, sex, age, region, survey wave) + 2 measures (preference share %, margin of error)

nodes.name: political_party
nodes.description: Political party used as a reporting category in the Party Preference Survey. Coded variable referencing the Swedish parliamentary parties. Acts as a key identifier dimension in both PSU table structures.
nodes.summary: Political party; key identifier dimension in PSU tables; coded using Swedish parliamentary party list

nodes.name: survey_wave
nodes.description: Survey wave or measurement occasion, for example May 2025. Identifies the specific data collection round in the twice-yearly Party Preference Survey. Acts as an identifier dimension providing the time axis in PSU tables.
nodes.summary: Survey wave; identifier dimension in PSU tables; identifies the measurement occasion (e.g. May 2025)

nodes.name: vote_share_percent
nodes.description: Estimated percentage of votes for a political party if a parliamentary election were held today. This is a measure variable in the election-today estimate table structure. Based on survey responses weighted for non-response and representativeness.
nodes.summary: Vote share; measure variable; estimated % of votes for a party if election held today

nodes.name: preference_share_percent
nodes.description: Estimated percentage of the electorate preferring a given political party, regardless of whether the person would vote. Measure variable in the party preference by demographic group table structure.
nodes.summary: Party preference share; measure variable; estimated % of electorate preferring a given party

nodes.name: margin_of_error
nodes.description: Uncertainty margin for the survey estimate, expressed in percentage points. Measure variable present in both PSU table structures. Reflects the sampling error associated with the estimate.
nodes.summary: Margin of error; measure variable; sampling uncertainty in percentage points for PSU estimates

nodes.name: sex (PSU)
nodes.description: Sex of the person, used as a demographic breakdown in PSU party preference tables. Coded variable; PSU-specific instance of the sex concept, sharing the same concept and code list as the LFS sex variable.
nodes.summary: Sex; demographic identifier dimension in PSU preference tables; coded (men/women)

nodes.name: age_group (PSU)
nodes.description: Age group used for presentation of political party preferences in PSU breakdowns. Coded variable; PSU-specific instance of the age concept, sharing the same concept and code list as the LFS age group variable.
nodes.summary: Age group; identifier dimension in PSU preference tables; coded age bands

nodes.name: region (PSU)
nodes.description: Geographical region used for breakdown of political party preferences in PSU demographic tables. Coded variable; PSU-specific instance of the region concept, sharing the same concept and code list as the LFS region variable.
nodes.summary: Region; identifier dimension in PSU preference tables; coded using Swedish regional classification

nodes.name: Political party
nodes.description: A political party used as a category in political preference and election statistics. In the Swedish context, this refers to the parties represented in or contesting the Riksdag.
nodes.summary: Political party as a statistical reporting category in preference and election surveys

nodes.name: Vote share
nodes.description: The estimated share of votes for a political party if a parliamentary election were held today. Derived from survey responses, weighted for representativeness.
nodes.summary: Estimated share of votes for a political party in an election-today scenario

nodes.name: Party preference
nodes.description: The political party that a person prefers the most, regardless of whether the person would actually vote in an election. Distinct from vote share, which applies to declared voting intention.
nodes.summary: The party a person prefers most, independent of stated voting intention

nodes.name: Margin of error
nodes.description: A measure of statistical uncertainty around a survey estimate, expressed in percentage points. Reflects sampling variability and is reported alongside estimated percentages in PSU publications.
nodes.summary: Statistical uncertainty around a survey estimate; expressed in percentage points

nodes.name: Survey wave
nodes.description: A specific measurement occasion in a recurring survey. In the PSU context, a survey wave corresponds to a biannual data collection period, for example May 2024 or May 2025.
nodes.summary: A specific measurement occasion in a recurring survey; e.g. May 2025 for PSU

nodes.name: Swedish political party code list (PSU demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for Swedish parliamentary parties, based on the categories used in SCB's Party Preference Survey publications.
nodes.summary: Swedish parliamentary party codes: C, L, M, KD, S, V, MP, SD, OTHER

nodes.name: Survey wave code list (PSU demo)
nodes.description: Simplified code list for PSU survey measurement occasions used in the demo.
nodes.summary: Survey wave codes: 2024M05=May 2024, 2025M05=May 2025

nodes.name: Population Statistics (Befolkningsstatistik)
nodes.description: Statistics describing the size, composition and change of the population registered in Sweden. Population Statistics (Befolkningsstatistik) is register-based, covering the total registered population without sampling error. It encompasses population stock (end-of-period headcounts), vital events (births, deaths, marriages, divorces) and migration (immigration, emigration, internal moves). Results are published quarterly for population stock and annually for full demographic breakdowns. Population Statistics feeds into Eurostat's demographic statistics and serves as the denominator for derived indicators in other statistical programmes such as LFS unemployment rates.
nodes.summary: Register-based programme covering population stock, births, deaths and migration for the total registered population in Sweden; denominator for many other statistical programmes

nodes.name: Population stock by region, sex, age and civil status
nodes.description: End-of-year population headcount broken down by region, sex, age group and civil status. Each observation represents the number of persons registered in Sweden at 31 December with a given combination of demographic and civil status characteristics. The dataset covers all regions from national level down to municipality level and is the primary source for population denominators used in rate calculations across official statistics.
nodes.summary: Annual end-of-year population headcount by region, sex, age group and civil status; primary denominator dataset for Swedish official statistics

nodes.name: Births by region, mother's age and sex of child
nodes.description: Annual dataset of live births in Sweden broken down by region of the mother, sex of the child and age group of the mother. Each observation represents the number of births with a given combination of characteristics. Used to calculate birth rates and fertility indicators including the Total Fertility Rate (TFR). Connects to Eurostat demographic statistics and indirectly to WHO vital statistics frameworks.
nodes.summary: Annual births dataset by region, mother's age group and sex of child; basis for birth rates and Total Fertility Rate calculation

nodes.name: Deaths by region, sex and age
nodes.description: Annual dataset of deaths in Sweden broken down by region, sex and age group of the deceased. Each observation represents the number of deaths with a given combination of characteristics. Used to calculate death rates, age-specific mortality and life expectancy. Connects to WHO via ICD-11 cause of death classification, though cause of death is not included in this aggregated table.
nodes.summary: Annual deaths dataset by region, sex and age group; basis for mortality rates and life expectancy; links to WHO via ICD-11 cause of death

nodes.name: Immigration and emigration by region, sex, age and country of birth
nodes.description: Annual dataset of immigration and emigration broken down by region, sex, age group and country of birth. Each observation represents the number of persons migrating with a given combination of characteristics. Covers both international immigration and emigration. Country of birth is the primary nativity dimension; citizenship is captured in related datasets. Enables analysis of the foreign-born population alongside population stock and labour market statistics.
nodes.summary: Annual migration dataset by region, sex, age and country of birth; covers international immigration and emigration; enables foreign-born population analysis

nodes.name: Population stock table structure
nodes.description: Data structure for the population stock table, capturing end-of-period population headcounts broken down by region, sex, age group, civil status and time period. Contains five identifier variables and one measure variable (population_count). Shares the population_count measure concept with the LFS programme, enabling cross-programme comparisons between register-based and survey-based population estimates.
nodes.summary: Structure for population stock table: 5 identifiers (region, sex, age, civil status, time) + 1 measure (population count); shares population_count concept with LFS

nodes.name: Vital events table structure
nodes.description: Shared data structure for vital events tables covering births and deaths. Contains four identifier variables (region, sex, age_group, time_period) and one measure variable (event_count). For births, age_group represents the mother's age; for deaths, it represents the age of the deceased. Both datasets share this structure, demonstrating how a common structure can serve multiple event types.
nodes.summary: Shared structure for births and deaths tables: 4 identifiers (region, sex, age group, time) + 1 measure (event count); shared across birth and death datasets

nodes.name: Migration table structure
nodes.description: Data structure for the migration table, capturing immigration and emigration counts broken down by region, sex, age group, country of birth and time period. Contains five identifier variables and one measure variable (migrant_count). The country_of_birth dimension is the key new addition relative to the population stock and vital events structures.
nodes.summary: Structure for migration table: 5 identifiers (region, sex, age, country of birth, time) + 1 measure (migrant count); introduces country of birth dimension

nodes.name: region (Pop)
nodes.description: Geographical region used for breakdown in Population Statistics. Coded variable covering Sweden from national level down to municipality (kommun) level. Acts as an identifier dimension across all population datasets. Population statistics use a finer regional granularity than LFS, extending to individual municipalities.
nodes.summary: Region; identifier dimension in population tables; coded from national to municipality level

nodes.name: sex (Pop)
nodes.description: Sex of the person, used as a demographic breakdown in population statistics tables. Coded variable; population-specific instance of the sex concept, sharing the same concept and code list as the LFS and PSU sex variables.
nodes.summary: Sex; demographic identifier dimension in population tables; coded (men/women)

nodes.name: age_group (Pop)
nodes.description: Age group used for presentation of population data. Coded variable; population-specific instance of the age concept. In population stock tables, single-year ages are available; aggregated tables use standard age bands. Shares the age concept and demo code list with LFS and PSU.
nodes.summary: Age group; identifier dimension in population tables; coded age bands

nodes.name: time_period (Pop)
nodes.description: Reference year or quarter for the population observation. Acts as the time axis identifier dimension in all population statistics tables.
nodes.summary: Time period; identifier dimension in population tables; reference year or quarter

nodes.name: population_count (Pop)
nodes.description: Number of persons registered in Sweden with a given combination of demographic characteristics at the reference date. Measure variable in the population stock table. Register-based count without sampling error; shares the Population count concept with the LFS programme where it is a survey-based estimate, enabling cross-programme comparison of measurement methods.
nodes.summary: Population count; measure variable in population stock table; register-based headcount sharing the Population count concept with LFS

nodes.name: civil_status
nodes.description: Civil or marital status of a person at the reference date. Coded variable used as an identifier dimension in the population stock table. Standard categories are: unmarried, married, divorced and widowed. In Sweden, registered partnership (sambo) is tracked separately from legal civil status.
nodes.summary: Civil status; identifier dimension in population stock table; coded (unmarried, married, divorced, widowed)

nodes.name: country_of_birth
nodes.description: The country in which a person was born. Coded variable using ISO 3166-1 country codes. Acts as an identifier dimension in the migration table and is a key nativity variable in population and labour market statistics. Country of birth is a standard Eurostat demographic variable enabling cross-country comparisons of migration and integration.
nodes.summary: Country of birth; identifier dimension in migration table; coded using ISO 3166-1; key nativity variable across demographic and labour market statistics

nodes.name: event_count
nodes.description: Number of vital events (births or deaths) in a given period with a specified combination of characteristics. Measure variable shared across the births and deaths datasets via the vital events table structure. For births, counts the number of live births; for deaths, counts the number of deaths.
nodes.summary: Event count; measure variable in vital events tables; number of births or deaths in the reference period

nodes.name: migrant_count
nodes.description: Number of persons immigrating to or emigrating from Sweden in a given period with a specified combination of characteristics. Measure variable in the migration table structure. Covers both international immigration and emigration depending on the direction of movement captured in the dataset.
nodes.summary: Migrant count; measure variable in migration table; number of immigrants or emigrants in the reference period

nodes.name: Civil status
nodes.description: A person's marital or civil status at a given point in time. Standard categories in Swedish population statistics are: unmarried (ogift), married (gift), divorced (skild) and widowed (änka/änkling). Civil status is a key demographic variable in population stock tables and is used to derive household composition indicators.
nodes.summary: Marital or civil status of a person; standard categories are unmarried, married, divorced and widowed

nodes.name: Country of birth
nodes.description: The country in which a person was born. A standard nativity variable in demographic and labour market statistics, coded using ISO 3166-1. Country of birth is distinct from citizenship and is used by Eurostat and SCB to measure the foreign-born population and migration patterns.
nodes.summary: Country where a person was born; coded using ISO 3166-1; key nativity variable across demographic and labour market statistics

nodes.name: Vital event
nodes.description: A demographic occurrence that affects the size or composition of the population: a live birth, a death, a marriage or a divorce. Vital events are the primary inputs to population change calculations. In Swedish population statistics, births and deaths are the most commonly analysed vital event types.
nodes.summary: A demographic occurrence affecting population composition: birth, death, marriage or divorce

nodes.name: Migration
nodes.description: Movement of persons across a border resulting in a change of usual residence. Includes international immigration (arrival in Sweden) and emigration (departure from Sweden). Migration is a key component of population change alongside natural increase (births minus deaths).
nodes.summary: Movement of persons across a border resulting in a change of usual residence; includes immigration and emigration

nodes.name: Life expectancy
nodes.description: The average number of years a person of a given age can be expected to live, calculated from age-specific mortality rates. Life expectancy at birth is the most commonly cited summary measure of population health and mortality. It is derived from deaths and population stock data and is reported by SCB, Eurostat and WHO.
nodes.summary: Average years of life remaining for a person of a given age; derived from age-specific mortality rates; reported by SCB, Eurostat and WHO

nodes.name: Civil status code list (Pop demo)
nodes.description: Code list for civil or marital status in Swedish population statistics.
nodes.summary: Civil status codes: OG=Unmarried, G=Married, SK=Divorced, AE=Widowed

nodes.name: Country of birth code list (Pop demo)
nodes.description: Simplified demo code list for country of birth, based on ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Includes a selection of the most common countries of birth in Swedish population statistics.
nodes.summary: Country of birth codes (ISO 3166-1 demo subset): SE, FI, PL, SY, SO, OTHER
